Mission townhomes for sale: ground-level homes in strata buildings. The Fraser Valley Real Estate Board benchmark for townhomes in Mission was $606,100 in October 2026 (-6.1% over a year). Before you offer, read the strata documents: the depreciation report, meeting minutes, bylaws and fees.
Mission townhomes sold, November 2025 to October 2026

65 townhomes sold in Mission with a median price of $679,900 (the middle half sold between $635,000 and $709,900), taking a median of 25 days to sell at 98.6% of the last list price; 3% sold above list. They had a median $444 per square foot, a median year built of 2021 and a median strata fee of $349 a month.

Mission Townhomes: streets and boundaries

items.t: Mission townhomes sit inside the City of Mission, under the Official Community Plan's Urban Residential Townhouse designation, which is the plan category that separates townhouse ground from the Urban Residential and Suburban Residential designations around it.

The growth corridor for the form is Cedar Valley, in the city's north-central area: the City's Cedar Valley Local Area Plan (November 2019) is one of the planning documents the City's Development Cost Charge background report builds its growth projections on.

blocks.text: Mission Townhomes: the housing stock

items.t: Mission creates townhouse zoning project by project: at 32909, 32919 and 32939 Cherry Avenue in Cedar Valley, the City processed a new Comprehensive Development 53 Zone (CD53) to allow 74 homes consisting of townhouses and back-to-back townhouses, on land zoned Suburban 20 (S20) under an Attached Multiunit Residential Official Community Plan designation.

Back-to-back townhouses are a distinct form in Mission: City staff brought the form to Council in September 2021 as a new housing form for Mission, with examples from neighbouring municipalities, before the Cherry Avenue application used it.

blocks.text: Mission Townhomes: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Zoning is under City of Mission Zoning Bylaw 5949-2020, and townhouse projects that do not fit an existing zone proceed by a site-specific comprehensive development zone, as CD53 did on Cherry Avenue.

Zones previously restricted to single family or duplex dwellings are subject to the provincial small-scale multi-unit housing legislation the City has adopted, which affects the detached streets around a townhouse complex rather than the strata complex itself.

blocks.text: Mission Townhomes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Mission's middle tier changes school planning: École Heritage Park Middle School, 33700 Prentis Avenue, takes Grades 7 to 9, so a townhome family changes schools after Grade 6 and again after Grade 9.
Mission Library, 33247 Second Avenue, is the Fraser Valley Regional Library branch in the downtown core.
The Mission Leisure Centre, 7650 Grand Street, is the City's main recreation complex.
Mission Memorial Hospital is at 7324 Hurd Street, and the Mission Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at 304 – 32555 London Avenue, open 7 days a week, 9:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m.
Fraser River Heritage Park is on the City's heritage register as the site of the former St. Mary's Mission.
Two transit systems meet at one station: BC Transit runs Mission's local buses and TransLink runs the West Coast Express and the 701 at Mission City Station, and different fares apply to each system.

blocks.text: Mission Townhomes: development and new projects

items.t: 32909, 32919 and 32939 Cherry Avenue, Cedar Valley: rezoning from Suburban 20 (S20) to a new Comprehensive Development 53 Zone (CD53) for 74 homes of townhouses and back-to-back townhouses, applicant Archstone Architecture Ltd., on a 10,618-square-metre developable site in phase 2 of the Cedar Valley Plan, beside Griner Park and a school site. Status: staff report of February 7, 2022 recommended first and second reading — over 12 months old, check current status with the City.

Cedar Valley Local Area Plan (November 2019) is the plan framework the City's current Development Cost Charge update uses for this townhouse growth area. Status: plan in force in the City's 2024 Development Cost Charge background report (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: Mission Townhomes: costs and taxes

items.t: The townhome-specific utility point is what does not apply: Mission's 2026 flat-rate utility fees total $1,892.28 per single family home (water $641.76, sanitary sewer $786.60, garbage $166.92, recycling and compostables $297.00), and the higher with-secondary-dwelling total of $3,207.60 cannot apply to a townhouse, because suites are not permitted in townhouses or rowhomes in Mission.
Mission bills utilities as a flat rate on the annual property tax notice for serviced homes, rather than metering most homes, and metered homes are billed water and sewer quarterly.

blocks.text: Mission Townhomes: getting around

items.t: BC Transit's Central Fraser Valley routes in Mission are 31 Valley Connector, 32 West Heights, 33 Cedar Valley, 34 East Side, 35 Hatzic and 39 Shopper Shuttle.

Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) runs east–west through the city and crosses the Fraser River to Abbotsford on the Mission Bridge (Highway 11), and Dewdney Trunk Road runs along the north side of the city toward Maple Ridge.
Mission City Station is the West Coast Express terminus, at 33200 North Railway Avenue.

blocks.text: Mission Townhomes: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the dike and flood frame on south-side complexes: the Fraser River floodplain runs along the city's south edge, low areas such as Hatzic Prairie are protected by the Dewdney Dyke system, and the City's tax rates page states additional taxes are levied for diking on top of the municipal, school, regional district and BC Assessment levies.

Check the zone, not the marketing form name: a Mission townhouse project may sit in a site-specific comprehensive development zone such as CD53, whose permitted forms (including back-to-back units) are written in that zone's own text in Zoning Bylaw 5949-2020.
Agricultural Land Reserve status on the city's rural edges is per-parcel on the Agricultural Land Commission's mapping.
